assumptions: Templates: synthetic headers (nonce_atlas::synthetic) and their 8 BIP320 version-rolled variants, so each group of 8 shares prev hash, merkle root, time and bits and differs in its midstate.
A hit at k bits: the hash, read as Bitcoin's 256-bit number, has >= k leading zero bits (probability exactly 2^-k per nonce for a random function).

Templates are compared at a shallow target (k bits) and a deeper one (k + deep bits). An effect present only at the real block target (~76 bits) and at neither of these is outside what this run can see.

Selection: the top `select` fraction of templates by even-nonce hits (ties by index). Under the null their odd-nonce hits are Poisson(m * nonces/2 * 2^-k) whatever the selection did; A = observed / expected.
Dispersion: D = sum (c - lambda)^2 / lambda over templates with the exact lambda, against chi-square(T); valid for large lambda (quick runs only check the pipeline).
64 rounds run on the GPU (kernel v3, every hit re-hashed on the CPU); reduced rounds cut all three compressions to r rounds and are positive controls, never evidence about 64 rounds.
Nonces 0..2^nonce_bits in order; reduced rounds use a smaller range, where the 4-round map is known to be far from random.
Significance: Bonferroni over the four primary tests of every round count.
baseline: Any template hits with probability 2^-k per nonce, so choosing templates gives A = 1 and leaves the expected work per block unchanged.
conclusion: REDUCED-ROUND ONLY: deviations were detected only for reduced-round variants. These say nothing about full 64-round SHA-256/SHA-256d and give no mining advantage; full-round configurations (where tested) showed no deviation. 4 rounds (256 templates x 2^24 nonces, k = 12): dispersion D/df = 1044480.0000 (p = 0.000e0, template rate SD <= 15.9687 at 95%); even/odd r = 1.0000 (p = 0.000e0); top 10% by even-nonce hits on odd nonces: A = 9.8462 (9.8196..9.8728) at 12 bits, A = 9.8462 (9.4289..10.2819) at 20 bits; deviation at the Bonferroni level. 5 rounds (256 templates x 2^24 nonces, k = 12): dispersion D/df = 0.8966 (p = 2.366e-1, template rate SD <= 0.0032 at 95%); even/odd r = -0.0415 (p = 5.094e-1); top 10% by even-nonce hits on odd nonces: A = 0.9974 (0.9889..1.0059) at 12 bits, A = 0.9327 (0.8104..1.0735) at 20 bits; no deviation. 6 rounds (256 templates x 2^24 nonces, k = 12): dispersion D/df = 0.8822 (p = 1.739e-1, template rate SD <= 0.0026 at 95%); even/odd r = -0.0027 (p = 9.663e-1); top 10% by even-nonce hits on odd nonces: A = 0.9958 (0.9874..1.0043) at 12 bits, A = 0.9231 (0.8014..1.0632) at 20 bits; no deviation. 8 rounds (256 templates x 2^24 nonces, k = 12): dispersion D/df = 0.7721 (p = 5.506e-3, template rate SD <= 0.0000 at 95%); even/odd r = -0.0763 (p = 2.239e-1); top 10% by even-nonce hits on odd nonces: A = 0.9932 (0.9848..1.0017) at 12 bits, A = 0.9471 (0.8238..1.0889) at 20 bits; no deviation. 64 rounds (2048 templates x 2^32 nonces, k = 20): dispersion D/df = 0.9555 (p = 1.515e-1, template rate SD <= 0.0013 at 95%); even/odd r = -0.0100 (p = 6.495e-1); top 10% by even-nonce hits on odd nonces: A = 1.0008 (0.9978..1.0039) at 20 bits, A = 1.0073 (0.9599..1.0571) at 28 bits; no deviation. Mining: choosing templates by their measured hit rate gives at most A = 1.0039 (95% upper bound) at 64 rounds; the expected work per block is unchanged.

dataset.description: Group g: nonce_atlas::synthetic(seed ^ 0x1ac4, g); template 8g + m: that header version-rolled by m (Work::version_rolled).

hypothesis: The probability that SHA256d(header) meets a target depends on the block template (merkle root, version), which the miner chooses for free: hit counts over whole nonce spaces vary between templates more than Poisson, and templates selected for many hits on even nonces also hit more often on odd nonces, at the selection target and at a deeper one.
methodology: Enumerate every nonce of every template; count hits at k and k + deep bits by nonce parity. Per round count: dispersion D of the totals (two-sided chi-square, plus a 95% upper bound on the template-to-template SD of the hit rate), Pearson r of even vs odd counts (Fisher z), and the top `select` fraction by even hits re-measured on odd nonces (and the reverse) with Wilson intervals and exact Poisson p-values.
name: Template luck: hit-rate spread between block templates, selected on even nonces and measured on odd ones
null_hypothesis: Every template's hit count over its nonce space is Poisson(nonces * 2^-k), independent between templates and between even and odd nonces: choosing templates does not change P(hash <= target).

reproduction.method: not run in-process for this kind; use `bmr research reproduce <id>`

verification.method: template 0 recounted with verification::independent::Sha256 (own constants, own compression): every nonce of the reduced-round range, and every nonce below 2^check_bits at 64 rounds compared hit for hit with the GPU
